hypotheses.claim: Switching from concentric rings to a 5x5 grid plus one additional circle will significantly improve sum_radii and target_ratio.
hypotheses.mechanism: Concentric rings are generally less efficient for square packing than grid-like or hexagonal patterns, especially for n=26. A 5x5 grid provides a better initial distribution, and fixing the bug of only 25 circles will allow all 26 to contribute.

hypotheses.claim: Introducing an iterative repulsion process for circle centers will further increase sum_radii and target_ratio.
hypotheses.mechanism: The repulsion method dynamically adjusts center positions to maximize distances between circles, allowing them to expand more without overlap, thus utilizing available space more effectively.

hypotheses.claim: Iterating the radius shrinkage process in compute_max_radii will ensure tighter packing and higher sum_radii.
hypotheses.mechanism: A single pass of shrinkage might not fully resolve all overlaps, especially for a complex packing. Multiple iterations allow radii to relax into their maximum possible sizes without overlap, globally optimizing.

hypotheses.claim: Proportional scaling in compute_max_radii is suboptimal; a greedy approach preserves larger radii.
